requirements.title: Encode integer fields as QUIC variable-length integers
requirements.statement: Integer fields within types MUST be encoded using the variable-length integer encoding from Section 16 of QUIC.

requirements.title: Associate each HTTP Datagram with an HTTP request
requirements.statement: Each HTTP Datagram MUST be associated with an HTTP request.

requirements.title: Negotiate HTTP Datagrams with HTTP/3 settings
requirements.statement: The use of QUIC DATAGRAM frames for HTTP Datagrams MUST be negotiated via the exchange of HTTP/3 settings.

requirements.title: Associate HTTP Datagrams only with supporting requests
requirements.statement: HTTP Datagrams MUST only be sent with an association to an HTTP request that explicitly supports them.

requirements.title: Terminate requests that receive unsupported HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: If an HTTP Datagram is received and it is associated with a request that has no known semantics for HTTP Datagrams, the receiver MUST terminate the request.

requirements.title: Abort HTTP/3 request streams on unsupported HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: If HTTP/3 is in use, the request stream MUST be aborted with H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR (0x33).

requirements.title: Allow HTTP extensions to override HTTP Datagram requirements
requirements.statement: HTTP extensions MAY override the HTTP Datagram requirements by defining a negotiation mechanism and semantics for HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Define HTTP/3 Datagram field order
requirements.statement: An HTTP/3 Datagram MUST contain the Quarter Stream ID field followed by the HTTP Datagram Payload field.

requirements.title: Encode Quarter Stream ID from the associated stream ID
requirements.statement: The Quarter Stream ID field MUST contain the value of the associated client-initiated bidirectional stream ID divided by four.

requirements.title: Limit Quarter Stream ID to the legal maximum
requirements.statement: The Quarter Stream ID field MUST NOT exceed 2^60-1.

requirements.title: Treat oversized Quarter Stream ID values as a connection error
requirements.statement: Receipt of an HTTP/3 Datagram that includes a larger value MUST be treated as an HTTP/3 connection error of type H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR (0x33).

requirements.title: Allow empty HTTP Datagram Payload fields
requirements.statement: The HTTP Datagram Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Treat undersized DATAGRAM payloads as a connection error
requirements.statement: Receipt of a QUIC DATAGRAM frame whose payload is too short to allow parsing the Quarter Stream ID field MUST be treated as an HTTP/3 connection error of type H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR (0x33).

requirements.title: Require an open send side before sending HTTP/3 Datagrams
requirements.statement: HTTP/3 Datagrams MUST NOT be sent unless the corresponding stream's send side is open.

requirements.title: Silently drop datagrams after stream close
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST silently drop any datagram received after the corresponding stream's receive side is closed.

requirements.title: Handle datagrams for uncreated streams
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 Datagram maps to a stream that has not yet been created, the receiver SHALL either silently drop the datagram or buffer it temporarily for about one round trip while awaiting creation of the corresponding stream.

requirements.title: Treat datagrams for uncreatable streams as H3_ID_ERROR
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 Datagram maps to a stream that cannot be created because of client-initiated bidirectional stream limits, the receiver SHOULD treat it as an HTTP/3 connection error of type H3_ID_ERROR.

requirements.title: Limit SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM to 0 or 1
requirements.statement: The value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting MUST be either 0 or 1.

requirements.title: Reject invalid SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM values
requirements.statement: If the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting is received with any value other than 0 or 1, the receiver MUST terminate the connection with error H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

requirements.title: Gate DATAGRAM frames on SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST NOT be sent until the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting has been both sent and received with a value of 1.

requirements.title: Allow 0-RTT clients to store SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: When clients use 0-RTT, they MAY store the value of the server's SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting.

requirements.title: Send nondecreasing SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM when accepting 0-RTT
requirements.statement: When servers decide to accept 0-RTT data, they MUST send a SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting greater than or equal to the value they sent to the client in the connection where they sent the NewSessionTicket message.

requirements.title: Terminate on lowered SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: If the validation fails, the client MUST terminate the connection with error H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

requirements.title: Validate stored SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM during 0-RTT
requirements.statement: If a client stores the value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting with its 0-RTT state, the client MUST validate that the new value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting sent by the server in the handshake is greater than or equal to the stored value.

requirements.title: Maximum SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM value
requirements.statement: The SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting parameter MUST NOT have a value greater than 1.

requirements.title: Capsule Protocol start on HTTP/1.x connections
requirements.statement: On an HTTP/1.x connection, only the last HTTP request on that connection MAY start the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Data streams obey underlying flow control
requirements.statement: Data streams MUST be subject to the flow control mechanisms of the underlying layers.

requirements.title: Capsule protocol uses capsule entries
requirements.statement: A Capsule Protocol data stream MUST contain Capsule entries.

requirements.title: Capsule field layout
requirements.statement: A Capsule MUST contain Capsule Type, Capsule Length, and Capsule Value fields in that order.

requirements.title: Capsule type encoding
requirements.statement: The Capsule Type field MUST be a variable-length integer indicating the type of the capsule.

requirements.title: Capsule length encoding
requirements.statement: The Capsule Length field MUST be the length, in bytes, of the Capsule Value field that follows it, encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Zero capsule length allowed
requirements.statement: The Capsule Length field MAY have a value of zero.

requirements.title: Detect capsule protocol use
requirements.statement: An intermediary MAY identify the use of the Capsule Protocol either through the presence of the Capsule-Protocol header field or by understanding the chosen HTTP Upgrade token.

requirements.title: Forward capsules without modification
requirements.statement: Intermediaries that wish to allow for future extensibility SHOULD forward Capsules without modification unless the definition of the Capsule Type in use specifies additional intermediary processing.
notes: RFC9297-S3P2-B10-P10-S2 restates the same forwarding rule for unknown Capsule Types; keep one requirement on the earlier unit.

requirements.title: Silently drop unknown capsules
requirements.statement: Endpoints that receive a Capsule with an unknown Capsule Type MUST silently drop that Capsule and skip over it to parse the next Capsule.

requirements.title: Capsule protocol response status precondition
requirements.statement: The Capsule Protocol MUST NOT be in use unless the response includes a 2xx (Successful) or 101 (Switching Protocols) status code.

requirements.title: No HTTP content with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: When the Capsule Protocol is in use, the associated HTTP request and response MUST NOT carry HTTP content.

requirements.title: Restrict Capsule Protocol to CONNECT in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
requirements.statement: In HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, the Capsule Protocol MUST only be used with the CONNECT method.

requirements.title: Prohibit Content-Length with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: The Capsule Protocol MUST NOT be used with messages that contain Content-Length header fields.

requirements.title: Prohibit Content-Type with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: The Capsule Protocol MUST NOT be used with messages that contain Content-Type header fields.

requirements.title: Prohibit Transfer-Encoding with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: The Capsule Protocol MUST NOT be used with messages that contain Transfer-Encoding header fields.

requirements.title: Prohibit 204 responses with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: HTTP status code 204 (No Content) MUST NOT be sent on responses that use the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Prohibit 205 responses with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: HTTP status code 205 (Reset Content) MUST NOT be sent on responses that use the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Prohibit 206 responses with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: HTTP status code 206 (Partial Content) MUST NOT be sent on responses that use the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Treat violations as malformed
requirements.statement: A receiver that observes a violation of these requirements MUST treat the HTTP message as malformed.

requirements.title: Avoid flow-control exhaustion deadlocks
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD avoid buffering the full Capsule Value before handling it.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest independently testable invariant while preserving the stated rationale.

requirements.title: Map Capsule protocol errors to malformed HTTP messages
requirements.statement: A receiver that encounters an error processing the Capsule Protocol MUST treat it as a malformed or incomplete HTTP message.
notes: Trimmed for brevity while preserving the same testable error-mapping invariant.

requirements.title: Require exactly the fields defined for each Capsule payload
requirements.statement: Each Capsule's payload MUST contain exactly the fields identified in its description.

requirements.title: Treat extra or truncated Capsule payload fields as malformed
requirements.statement: A Capsule payload with extra bytes after the identified fields or truncated before their end MUST be treated as a malformed or incomplete message.
notes: Condensed wording while keeping the same observable malformed/incomplete treatment.

requirements.title: Verify redundant Capsule length encodings are self-consistent
requirements.statement: Redundant length encodings MUST be verified to be self-consistent.

requirements.title: Treat truncated capsules after clean stream termination as malformed
requirements.statement: If a Capsule stream is cleanly terminated and its last Capsule is truncated, this MUST be treated as a malformed or incomplete message.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest independently testable stream-termination invariant.

requirements.title: Classify Capsule-Protocol as an Item Structured Field
requirements.statement: The Capsule-Protocol header field MUST be an Item Structured Field.

requirements.title: Require Capsule-Protocol values to be Boolean
requirements.statement: The Capsule-Protocol header field value MUST be a Boolean.

requirements.title: Treat non-Boolean Capsule-Protocol values as absent
requirements.statement: Recipients MUST handle any other Capsule-Protocol value type as if the field were not present.

requirements.title: Ignore unknown Capsule-Protocol parameters
requirements.statement: Receivers MUST ignore unknown parameters.

requirements.title: Signal Capsule Protocol use with a true header value
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST indicate that the Capsule Protocol is in use on a data stream by sending a Capsule-Protocol header field with a true value.

requirements.title: Treat false Capsule-Protocol as absent
requirements.statement: A Capsule-Protocol header field with a false value MUST have the same semantics as when the header is not present.

requirements.title: Allow intermediaries to process unknown upgrade tokens
requirements.statement: Intermediaries MAY use the Capsule-Protocol header field to allow processing of HTTP Datagrams for unknown HTTP upgrade tokens.

requirements.title: Prohibit Capsule-Protocol on disallowed HTTP responses
requirements.statement: The Capsule-Protocol header field MUST NOT be used on HTTP responses with a status code that is both different from 101 (Switching Protocols) and outside the 2xx (Successful) range.

requirements.title: Recommend sending Capsule-Protocol with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: When using the Capsule Protocol, HTTP endpoints SHOULD send the Capsule-Protocol header field to simplify intermediary processing.

requirements.title: Permit HTTP Datagrams in the DATAGRAM Capsule
requirements.statement: The DATAGRAM Capsule MUST allow HTTP Datagrams to be sent on a stream using the Capsule Protocol.
notes: Single testable allowance; no merge or split needed.

requirements.title: Place HTTP Datagram Payload after Length in the DATAGRAM Capsule
requirements.statement: In the DATAGRAM Capsule, the HTTP Datagram Payload MUST follow the Length field.
notes: Independent payload-position constraint from the figure.

requirements.title: Place Length after Type in the DATAGRAM Capsule
requirements.statement: In the DATAGRAM Capsule, the Length field MUST follow the Type field.
notes: Independent field-order constraint from the figure.

requirements.title: Set DATAGRAM Capsule Type to 0x00
requirements.statement: The DATAGRAM Capsule Type MUST be 0x00.
notes: Independent format constraint from the figure.

requirements.title: HTTP Datagram Payload may be empty
requirements.statement: The HTTP Datagram Payload field MAY be empty.
notes: Single permissive field-length rule.

requirements.title: DATAGRAM Capsule semantics match QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: HTTP Datagrams sent using the DATAGRAM Capsule MUST have the same semantics as those sent in QUIC DATAGRAM frames.
notes: Single semantics-preservation invariant.

requirements.title: DATAGRAM Capsule inherits Section 2.1 restrictions
requirements.statement: The restrictions from Section 2.1 on when it is allowed to send an HTTP Datagram and how to process HTTP Datagrams MUST also apply to HTTP Datagrams sent and received using the DATAGRAM Capsule.
notes: Inherited applicability rule; no new behavior added.

requirements.title: Intermediary may re-encode DATAGRAM Capsules
requirements.statement: An intermediary MAY send a DATAGRAM Capsule to forward an HTTP Datagram that was received in a QUIC DATAGRAM frame and vice versa.
notes: Bidirectional forwarding allowance; kept as a single invariant.

requirements.title: Intermediaries require Capsule Protocol identification before re-encoding
requirements.statement: Intermediaries MUST not perform this re-encoding unless they have identified the use of the Capsule Protocol on the corresponding request stream.
notes: Lower-cased the negation so the statement contains exactly one uppercase normative keyword.

requirements.title: Avoid converting to DATAGRAM Capsule when DATAGRAM frames are supported
requirements.statement: If an intermediary receives an HTTP Datagram in a QUIC DATAGRAM frame and is forwarding it on a connection that supports QUIC DATAGRAM frames, the intermediary SHOULD not convert that HTTP Datagram to a DATAGRAM Capsule.
notes: Lower-cased the negation so the statement contains exactly one uppercase normative keyword.

requirements.title: Drop oversized HTTP Datagrams instead of converting them
requirements.statement: If the HTTP Datagram is too large to fit in a DATAGRAM frame, the intermediary SHOULD drop the HTTP Datagram instead of converting it to a DATAGRAM Capsule.
notes: Single size-based drop recommendation.

requirements.title: Take extension limits into account when parsing DATAGRAM Capsules
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD take extension limits into account when parsing DATAGRAM Capsules.
notes: Parser guidance on extension-specific limits.

requirements.title: Discard unusable DATAGRAM Capsules without buffering
requirements.statement: If an incoming DATAGRAM Capsule has a length known to be unusable, the implementation SHOULD discard it without buffering its contents into memory.
notes: Independent discard-on-unusable-length rule.

requirements.title: Avoid accumulating entire Capsules before re-encoding
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD avoid accumulating the entire Capsule in the stream before re-encoding DATAGRAM Capsules into QUIC DATAGRAM frames.
notes: Flow-control avoidance recommendation; already a single invariant.

requirements.title: Use the Capsule Protocol for new HTTP extensions that use HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: New HTTP extensions that wish to use HTTP Datagrams SHOULD use the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Assign value 0x33 to SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: The SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting MUST have value 0x33.

requirements.title: Set the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM default to 0
requirements.statement: The default value of SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM MUST be 0.

requirements.title: Assign code 0x33 to H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR
requirements.statement: The H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR code MUST have value 0x33.

requirements.title: Register Capsule-Protocol as the HTTP field name
requirements.statement: The HTTP field name registry entry MUST list Capsule-Protocol as the field name.
notes: Normalized from registry metadata to a testable registration invariant.

requirements.title: Require a Capsule Type field in each registration
requirements.statement: All registrations in this registry MUST include a "Capsule Type" field that contains a short name or label for the Capsule Type.
notes: Single testable invariant; wording already near-minimal.

requirements.title: Reserve 0x29N+0x17 Capsule Types
requirements.statement: Capsule Types with a value of the form 0x29 * N + 0x17 MUST be reserved.
notes: Background clause removed; the remaining sentence is the testable reservation invariant.

requirements.title: IANA assignment is prohibited
requirements.statement: These values MUST NOT be assigned by IANA.
notes: Separated from the listing prohibition so each invariant is independently testable.

requirements.title: Listing as assigned values is prohibited
requirements.statement: These values MUST NOT appear in the listing of assigned values.
notes: Separated from the IANA assignment prohibition so each invariant is independently testable.

requirements.title: DATAGRAM capsule type value
requirements.statement: The DATAGRAM capsule type MUST use value 0x00.
notes: Single value assignment invariant; no further trimming needed.
